name: Jellyfin
author: Plinth
description: Who's streaming what from your Jellyfin server and the titles that just landed in the library — or a player that streams a title straight to the panel. Read from Jellyfin's own API, because the web app refuses to render inside a frame.

properties.name: baseUrl
properties.label: Jellyfin address
properties.help: The address you open Jellyfin on, including the port — typically http://<server>:8096. Use an https:// address if you have one: every poll sends the API key with the request, and over plain http that credential crosses your network in the clear.

properties.name: apiKey
properties.label: API key
properties.help: A Jellyfin API key: Administration → Dashboard → Advanced → API Keys → +. An API key carries server-wide rights — it can read every library and see every user's activity — so treat it like the server's password.

properties.name: certValidation
properties.label: Certificate check (https)
properties.help: Only matters for an https:// address. Every request carries the API key, so by default the certificate must prove the server is really yours before anything is sent. Allow self-signed trades that proof away, and only works when the address is a literal LAN IP (like https://192.168.1.20) or localhost — at a named address the certificate must be one this PC trusts. Player-view playback accepts a self-signed certificate at those same LAN addresses regardless of this setting: a self-hosted server rarely has a signed certificate, and on the same LAN that is no more exposed than the plain-http default Jellyfin ships with.

properties.name: view
properties.label: View
properties.help: Server overview lists every active stream plus the recently-added shelf. Player turns the tile into a little theater: tap a recently-added title and it plays right on the panel. Panel playback is untracked — an API key belongs to the server, not to a user, so it does not mark titles watched or move anyone's resume position. Place two copies of the widget to have both.
